children: Readers of a national daily were taken by surprise last week when they turned the front page and found a talking newspaper. Hyundai’s ad for Bayon, its new mid-sized SUV, was packed with innovation using sound technology in a medium that is usually read and not heard. The ad, running into four pages, carried an image of a button on one of the pages.

When pressed, an AI voice outlined the car’s features and intelligent technology. Created by Innocean and Havas Media, the disruptive audio format in print brings alive the car’s AI features. Truly a masterpiece, it prompted delighted readers to go on social media and declare that ‘Print is back’.

Spotify’s Deepavali campaign, featuring the much-loved cast of Gullak, under the tagline ‘Diwali ki taiyaari fun banao, Spotify chalao’, shows how a song can turn the task of making laddoos, drawing a rangoli or untangling fairy lights into shared family moments. The three one-minute films bring the festival prep activities to life through the Mishra family, known for its everyday bickering and warmth. So ‘Taambdi Chaamdi’ forms the backdrop to ladoo-making, ‘Chaiya Chaiya’ accompanies rangoli making and ‘Badan Pe Sitare’ lights up the attempt to untangle the lights. The family bickers over each chore until someone turns on Spotify, and it’s all fun thereon.

Sorry Sugar, the zero-added-sugar beverage brand, has launched its Deepavali campaign, ‘Yeh Diwali, Bina Cheeni Wali’, a high-energy song-and-dance film that changes the festive script. The brand puts indulgence at the centre of the conversation and challenges two long-standing perceptions — namely “healthy is boring”, and “sweetness is synonymous with sugar”. The campaign also introduces the Sorry Sugar assorted coffee gift set, which brings together the brand’s zero-added-sugar flavoured coffee premixes, a reusable organiser box and a complimentary frother.

Zomato’s digital Diwali ad features actor Saif Ali Khan getting irritated by the routine Diwali hampers he gets. He sarcastically says “Wow/” everytime someone presents him with a hamper with common gifts such as crockery, soaps and so on. His reaction changes when a Zomato delivery partner arrives with a Diwali hamper full of enticing food items. The premise being nothing beats a hamper from a mithai shop, bakery, or restaurant for Diwali. Zomato has also extended the Diwali hamper campaign through influencer collaborations, with creators featuring the food-led hampers as part of the festive campaign.

title: On the campaign trail. Sound on
